text: Next came a young man and a young woman called Trissie. <break time="0.8s" /> Both in the prime of youth. <break time="0.8s" /> And he remarked. <break time="0.8s" /> That it was lucky it was not Friday. <break time="0.8s" /> Since they made you pay sixpence on Fridays. <break time="0.8s" /> When she asked. <break time="0.8s" /> What sixpence mattered anyway. <break time="0.8s" /> And whether it was not worth sixpence. <break time="0.8s" /> He asked what she meant by it. <break time="0.8s" /> And she could only answer. <break time="0.8s" /> Oh, anything, I mean, you know what I mean. <break time="0.8s" /> After a pause. <break time="0.8s" /> The couple stood still on the edge of the flower bed. <break time="0.8s" /> And together pressed the end of her parasol. <break time="0.8s" /> Deep into the soft earth. <break time="0.8s" /> His hand resting on the top of hers. <break time="0.8s" /> Their short, insignificant words. <break time="0.8s" /> Were like short wings. <break time="0.8s" /> For a heavy body of meaning. <break time="0.8s" /> Too weak to carry it far. <break time="0.8s" /> And thus alighting awkwardly. <break time="0.8s" /> Upon the very common objects around them. <break time="0.8s" /> When he said. <break time="0.8s" /> That it was time they had their tea. <break time="0.8s" /> She asked with the oddest thrill of excitement. <break time="0.8s" /> Where one had ones tea. <break time="0.8s" /> Remembering orchids, a Chinese pagoda, and a crimson crested bird. <break time="0.8s" /> But he bore her on. <break time="0.8s" /> Thus one couple after another passed the flower bed. <break time="0.8s" /> With much the same irregular and aimless movement. <break time="0.8s" /> And they were enveloped. <break time="0.8s" /> In layer after layer of green blue vapor. <break time="0.8s" /> In which their bodies and colors slowly dissolved. <break time="0.8s" /> Voices, yes, wordless voices. <break time="0.8s" /> Broke the silence suddenly. <break time="0.8s" /> With deep contentment, passionate desire. <break time="0.8s" /> Or, in the voices of children, fresh surprise. <break time="0.8s" /> But in truth there was no silence at all. <break time="0.8s" /> All the time. <break time="0.8s" /> The motor buses were turning their wheels. <break time="0.8s" /> And the city murmured. <break time="0.8s" /> Like a vast nest of Chinese boxes of steel. <break time="0.8s" /> Above which voices cried aloud. <break time="0.8s" /> And myriads of flowers flashed their colors into the air.
